title: Give mayors a share of income tax
gist: West Yorkshire mayor Tracy Brabin and Milton Keynes North MP Chris Curtis argue Prime Minister Andy Burnham should assign combined authorities a share of income tax, arguing the binding constraint on English devolution is not political opposition but Whitehall's institutional incentive to hoard power. They also call for mayoral control over National Wealth Fund, Homes England and British Business Bank allocations, coterminous public service boundaries, and 'devolved diplomacy' capacity for regional investment attraction.

insights.claim: The main obstacle to English devolution is not political opponents but the British state itself, because Whitehall departments are structurally conditioned to accumulate power and accountability systems reward ministers for retaining rather than transferring decisions.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: Devolution announcements should be discounted unless they change accountability structures, not just budgets — the failure mode is institutional, not electoral.
insights.quote: Whitehall departments are conditioned to accumulate power, not disperse it. Accountability systems reward ministers for keeping a grip on decisions, not handing them over.
insights.locator: Burnham’s biggest challenge may not be Reform UK

insights.claim: Reform UK's flirtation with abolishing the Welsh Senedd shows devolution in the UK cannot be treated as an irreversible settlement.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: Devolved institutional arrangements carry reversal risk under a future right-wing government — relevant to long-dated regional infrastructure commitments.
insights.quote: Reform’s flirtation with abolishing the Welsh Senedd illustrates that devolution cannot be taken for granted
insights.locator: Burnham’s biggest challenge may not be Reform UK

insights.claim: England's devolution effort has repeatedly been Sisyphean, meaning momentum reverses the moment political attention lapses, so Burnham must move fast while momentum is with him.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: Timing matters more than design — the window for structural fiscal reform in the UK is narrow and front-loaded in the parliament.
insights.quote: Hesitate and, as for Sisyphus, the boulder will begin rolling downhill once again.
insights.locator: Andy Burnham has experience that few others

insights.claim: Assigning a share of income tax to England's combined authorities would fundamentally change the Whitehall-region relationship by creating a direct financial incentive for mayors to grow their local economies and giving them certainty to invest long-term.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: Regional revenue assignment would create genuinely growth-motivated subnational actors in the UK for the first time — watch for it in the next fiscal event.
insights.quote: Designed well, it would create a direct incentive for local leaders to grow their economies, while giving them the certainty to invest over the long term.
insights.locator: But these are the beginning, not the end

insights.claim: Two concrete fiscal devolution steps are already live in the UK: an overnight visitor levy allowing places to charge tourists for public services and infrastructure, and the Integrated Settlement giving combined authorities greater flexibility over how funding is spent.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: A UK overnight visitor levy is a direct new cost line for hotel and short-let operators in devolved city-regions.
insights.quote: The introduction of an overnight visitor levy will allow places to ensure tourists contribute to the public services and infrastructure they rely on.
insights.locator: As we have heard him make a powerful case

insights.claim: Until Labour entered government, successive UK administrations resisted meaningful fiscal autonomy for England's city-regions at almost every turn.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: The historical baseline of resistance means any actual tax-assignment delivery would be a genuine regime change rather than incrementalism.
insights.quote: successive administrations resisted meaningful fiscal autonomy for England’s city-regions at almost every turn
insights.locator: As we have heard him make a powerful case

insights.claim: The National Wealth Fund, Homes England and the British Business Bank invest in local economies but remain overwhelmingly directed from Whitehall, and mayors should get a far greater role in deciding where that capital goes.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: A shift in allocation authority over these three balance sheets would redirect UK public investment flows toward regional priorities — material for housebuilders and regional SMEs.
insights.quote: bodies such as the National Wealth Fund, Homes England and the British Business Bank remain overwhelmingly directed from Whitehall, even though they invest in local economies
insights.locator: The prime minister needs to radically rethink

insights.claim: Regional growth companies already operating in London and Greater Manchester provide a working template for mayoral-directed investment vehicles that could be replicated nationally.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: An existing proven vehicle lowers the implementation barrier, making replication a realistic near-term policy rather than a concept.
insights.quote: building on successful models already operating in London and Greater Manchester
insights.locator: Mayors should have a far greater role

insights.claim: Devolution must pass a 'Makerfield Test' — also framable as a Milton Keynes or Huddersfield test — meaning ordinary people must be able to see the benefits in daily life, not just in institutional architecture.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: A visible-outcomes test is the political survival condition for devolution; without it the reform reverses at the next election.
insights.quote: If devolution is to pass the “Makerfield Test”—which could also be called the “Milton Keynes” or “Huddersfield” test—people need to be able to see the benefits of devolution in their daily lives.
insights.locator: The same principle applies to public services

insights.claim: Public services must operate across the same boundaries as combined authorities so that policing, transport, health and economic development can work in concert, otherwise institutions optimise for their own budget lines rather than communities.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: Boundary coterminosity is the unglamorous precondition for devolution delivering measurable savings — a technical marker to watch in legislation.
insights.quote: A presumption in favour of “coterminous” public services may sound technocratic, but it is the difference between joined-up government and a web of public services that focus too much on their own resilience and budget lines
insights.locator: That, in turn, requires Whitehall to change

insights.claim: Temporary accommodation, children's social care and economic inactivity are the specific cross-institutional problems that no single local authority can solve and that mayoral strategic coordination is meant to address.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: These three areas are where devolved spending will concentrate — relevant to social housing, care providers and welfare-to-work contractors.
insights.quote: Temporary accommodation, children’s social care and economic inactivity all demand coordinated leadership across institutions and local authorities.
insights.locator: Through devolved powers, mayors have a role

insights.claim: UK mayors are already acting as international ambassadors attracting investment and forging overseas partnerships, but with a fraction of the support enjoyed by comparable regions in Germany, France and Australia.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: A capability gap versus German Länder and French regions in FDI attraction is an under-discussed reason UK regional investment lags.
insights.quote: Yet they do so with a fraction of the support enjoyed by comparable regions in countries such as Germany, France and Australia.
insights.locator: We also have an opportunity to think beyond England’s borders

insights.claim: West Yorkshire has the ambition and capacity to accelerate growth but remains constrained by Whitehall, while the South Midlands combined authority that Milton Keynes would join has been paused despite local leaders' appetite.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that the devolution pipeline is stalling in practice even under a devolution-committed government.
insights.quote: the South Midlands combined authority—which Milton Keynes will join—has been paused despite the appetite from local leaders

insights.claim: Burnham's government has made devolution the defining mission of the parliament, establishing Number 10 North and creating a National Economic Council with mayors at the table.
insights.speaker: Tracy Brabin, Chris Curtis
insights.so_what: Institutional signals of intent that give the devolution trade a policy tailwind — but the authors themselves treat these as insufficient without tax assignment.
insights.quote: establishing Number 10 North, creating a National Economic Council with mayors at the table
insights.locator: He has made a strong start
